title: Minimalist and intuitive interface
description: The mobile-application interface shall be minimalist and intuitive, achieving a System Usability Scale (SUS) score >= 70.
measurable_criterion: SUS score >= 70 (equivalent to 'Good' per Bangor et al. 2009)
verification_method: User study with the SUS questionnaire (n = 19 guardians)
source: Stakeholder interviews; literature (Brooke 1996; Bangor et al. 2008, 2009)

title: Non-intrusive form-factor
description: The IoT device shall be similar in form-factor and appearance to an everyday object familiar to the child (e.g. a toy), so that its presence does not disrupt the study routine.
measurable_criterion: Qualitative: the enclosure resembles an everyday object familiar to the child. Indicator measured: Statement 3 of the perception questionnaire ('The child did not perceive the presence of the device as intrusive'). The requirement specification (Online Resource 1, Section S5) sets no numerical threshold.
status: MEASURED. Statement 3: mean = 3.05, SD = 0.92, n = 21 (4 pairs disagreed or strongly disagreed, 10 neutral, 7 agreed). This is the lowest of the seven items and sits at the scale midpoint. Reported openly in Section 6 of the manuscript and carried into the discussion and future work; a child-facing instrument and an enclosure redesign are the planned actions. The value of 4.42 previously recorded here does not appear in the data and has been removed.

title: Mains-powered operation
description: The IoT device shall be powered from the domestic mains supply, given its intended fixed-location use for schoolwork.
measurable_criterion: Continuous operation >= 4 hours without interruption; automatic reboot within 30 s after a power outage
verification_method: Endurance test (integration lab); observed field operation
status: Implemented (mains-powered by design; no endurance-test report is deposited in this repository)

title: End-to-end data encryption
description: Personal and authentication data shall be encrypted end-to-end using cryptographic mechanisms compliant with the current recommendations of ISO/IEC 27001:2022. (Specification as recorded in Online Resource 1, Section S5.)
measurable_criterion: Encrypted transport for all personal and authentication data; encryption at rest; password derivation with an iteration-hard function
verification_method: Network inspection during deployment; code review
status: NOT IMPLEMENTED IN THE PROTOTYPE - DEFERRED BY DEPLOYMENT SCOPE. The requirement was specified for the eventual deployment of Torddis as a networked service. The prototype evaluated in the study was never deployed on a cloud or internet-facing server: it ran as a self-contained local system inside each household, so no personal or authentication datum traversed a network outside the home, and the cryptographic mechanisms were therefore judged unnecessary for the pilot. Residual risk, stated explicitly: within the household network the traffic travels over HTTP and is readable by any other device attached to it. The controls required before any networked deployment are specified in docs/security/deployment-security-plan.md and in Online Resource 1, Section S12; C1 (TLS 1.3), C2 (device and client authentication) and C7 (non-defeasible live-stream indicator) are blocking.

title: Recognition latency
description: The system shall achieve a mean end-to-end latency below 1.5 s for the person-recognition module and below 5 s for the drowsiness-detection module.
measurable_criterion: Mean latency (person recognition) < 1.5 s; mean latency (drowsiness detection) < 5.0 s; assessed event by event rather than on averages alone
verification_method: Instrumented latency measurement over the 108 recognition events recorded in the 19 monitored sessions
status: Verified (person: mean 0.639 s, SD 0.355, 100/101 true positives below the 1.5 s ceiling, single exception at 1.65 s; drowsiness: mean 1.943 s, SD 1.096, all 100 true positives below the 5 s ceiling, maximum 4.57 s)
